newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-AUSTRALIAN EVANS FULFILLS LIFELONG AMBITION.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-AUSTRALIAN EVANS FULFILLS LIFELONG AMBITION.

text.p: Australian champion jockey Jamie Evans fulfilled a lifelong dream on Wednesday when he won at the Cheltenham festival with a dramatic last-gasp win on the 16-1 Big Strand.

"He sprouted wings didn't he?" said the 27-year-old from Melbourne who timed his charge to perfection in the Coral Cup to land the hurdling prize by the shortest of short heads from the horse's stable companion Allegation.
Evans, whose thrilling victory was one of the most exquisitely timed triumphs ever seen on the gruelling Cheltenham hill said afterwards: "My timing isn't too bad, hey?"
For Evans, three times champion jockey in Australia, racing in England has been a real rollercoaster ride of mixed fortunes.
"This time last year at the festival I was being loaded into an ambulance with a broken femur," he said, recalling the 1996 festival which ended in catastrophe for him.
For Champion trainer Martin Pipe it was a third victory at the festival and he was quick to praise Evans, telling reporters: "He tells me he is brilliant and proved it today."
The globetrotting Evans has ridden winners in six countries and has one more burning ambition he wants to fulfill in Britain.

"I would love to avenge Chrisp's defeat by Red Rum in the Grand National," he said, keeping his fingers crossed that the all-conquering Pipe might offer him a ride in the race next month in Liverpool.
But on Wednesday he was savouring the delight of his thrilling victory saying: "To ride a festival winner is a dream come true."
Describing his victory in the giant field, Evans revealed he was no closer than 13th at the last bend and looked unlikely at the last hurdle to even run into a place.
"I bided my time and stuck to the inside. The Red Sea parted in the end and I was through."
